wicked.definition: Evil or mischievous by nature; morally reprehensible.

wide.definition: Having a large physical extent from side to side.

widower.definition: A man whose spouse has died (and who has not remarried); a man in relation to his late spouse; masculine of widow.

wife.definition: A married woman, especially in relation to her spouse.

wig.definition: A head of real or synthetic hair worn on the head to disguise baldness, for cultural or religious reasons, for fashion, or by actors to help them better resemble the character they are portraying.

wilde.definition: Form of wild (obsolete): Untamed; not domesticated.

will.definition: Used to express the future tense, sometimes with an implication of volition or determination when used in the first person. Compare shall.

willed.definition: Form of will (participle past): Used to express the future tense, sometimes with an implication of volition or determination when used in the first person. Compare shall.

wills.definition: Form of will (indicative present singular third-person): Used to express the future tense, sometimes with an implication of volition or determination when used in the first person. Compare shall.

windows.definition: Form of window (plural): An opening, usually covered by one or more panes of clear glass, to allow light and air from outside to enter a building or vehicle.

wool.definition: The hair of the sheep, llama and some other ruminants.

wore.definition: Form of wear (past): To have on.
